materials.sources: ENVIRONMENTAL PRODUCT DECLARATION FMI Fachverband Mineralwolleindustrie e.V.
materials.summary: Glass wool is a flexible, fibrous insulation commonly used in attics and walls, offering good thermal and sound insulation at a relatively low cost. It is breathable and works well in standard constructions, but it must be kept dry and properly installed to perform well. While it has low emissions in use, it can release fibres during installation and offers limited benefit for summer comfort or moisture buffering. It’s a reliable, conventional option where access and installation quality can be controlled.

www.nsai.ie/
materials.summary: EPS beads are commonly injected into wall cavities to provide even, gap-free insulation with minimal disruption, making them a popular retrofit solution in Ireland. They are water-resistant and perform well in exposed conditions, with low health risk once installed, but they do not regulate moisture or improve summer comfort. While technically recyclable, they are rarely recovered in practice. This is a low-risk, cost-effective upgrade for cavity walls, particularly in existing homes.

www.nsai.ie/
materials.summary: This is a pumped, cement-based insulation layer (often with EPS beads) used under floors to create a seamless, gap-free insulation base, making it excellent for reducing heat loss and thermal bridging. It’s very durable and has good indoor air quality once cured, but it does not regulate moisture or help with summer overheating, and it cannot be removed or recycled at end of life. It’s best suited where you want a robust, long-term floor solution with minimal installation risk, particularly in solid floor upgrades.

materials.name: Open cell Spray Foam
materials.sources:
Ökobaudat:
https://www.oekobaudat.de/OEKOBAU.DAT/datasetdetail/process.xhtml?uuid=b960f95d-466b-4014-9565-64e51407a364&version=20.24.070&lang=en
PUR rigid foam; hard foam, gross density: 30.0 kg/m^3

Ecovision: 3,0-5,0
Buildings Performance Institute Europe
materials.summary: Open cell spray foam expands to fill gaps, creating a highly airtight and breathable insulation layer, typically used in roofs. It can improve comfort and reduce drafts, especially in hard-to-insulate spaces, but installation quality is critical due to chemical emissions during application. It allows some moisture movement, which can be beneficial, but also requires careful design to avoid issues. It is not removable or recyclable, so it’s best used where other insulation methods are not feasible.

materials.name: Closed Cell spray foam
materials.sources:
Ökobaudat:
https://www.oekobaudat.de/OEKOBAU.DAT/datasetdetail/process.xhtml?uuid=355dbd58-78dc-45cc-be8a-43d66d117e15&version=20.24.070&lang=en
PIR high-density foam, gross density: 30.0 kg/m^3

Ecovision: 3,0-5,0
https://www.bpie.eu/
materials.summary: Closed cell spray foam is a dense, rigid insulation that provides high insulation value and acts as a vapour barrier, making it effective for sealing and strengthening structures. However, it can trap moisture if incorrectly applied, carries similar installation emission risks, and has no recycling or removal options at end of life. It also does little for summer comfort. This solution should be used cautiously and typically only where its specific properties (e.g. moisture barrier or structural support) are required.
